events.text: The night the Shadow Lodges come up from under the inns, you are woken by bells nobody is ringing on purpose. By dawn the river gates of {pw_kingdom} are theirs, and every stallholder in the market has a new landlord. A runner in a grey hood stops at your door, looks at you a long moment, and walks on.

choices.text: Bar the door and count what you have

effects.log: You count your stores twice and your friends once. Both are fewer than you would like.

choices.text: Follow the runner through the back lanes

effects.log: You follow the hood to a dye-works, and learn which door the Lodges use. It may be worth something.

choices.text: Go to the market and stand with the stallholders

effects.log: You stand with them while the Lodges collect. Nobody pays a copper more than they must, that day.

events.text: A guild-mother of {pw_kingdom} comes to you the morning after the Lodges take the river gates. "They poison wells they mean to sell water from," she says. "They pick every lock but the good ones. I hear your hands make good ones."

choices.text: Promise her your craft

effects.log: "Then we have a chance," she says, and writes your name in a book she keeps under her apron.

choices.text: Say you will think about it

effects.log: She nods. "Think quickly," she says. "They are not thinking slowly."

events.text: The Lodges send you a gift: a fine jar of plum wine and a note in a beautiful hand. "We admire your work. Make it for us, and the kingdoms will never trouble you again."

choices.text: Pour the wine out in the street

effects.log: You pour it out where the runners can see. The note you keep, to learn the hand.

choices.text: Keep the wine, and the note, and say nothing

effects.log: The jar stays sealed on a high shelf. The silence is noticed on both sides.

events.text: A child of the ferry-folk brings you a scrap of ledger she found in the river: names, sums, and one word over all of it, LODGE. Half the names are people you buy bread from.

choices.text: Burn it, and protect the names

effects.log: You burn it. Whatever those people owed, they owed it under a knife.

choices.text: Take it to the Wardens of the roads

effects.log: The Wardens thank you, and three cells close that week. Two stallholders never speak to you again.

events.text: Fire in the night: the Lodges burn a warehouse of grain to teach {pw_kingdom} what the price of bread will be. You are on the bucket line until dawn with people you do not know.

choices.text: Stay on the line to the last bucket

effects.log: By morning the fire is out and your hands are raw. Strangers nod to you in the street for a month.

choices.text: Go and find who lit it

effects.log: You find the runner who lit it asleep in a boat. You leave him for the Wardens, tied with his own rope.

events.text: A Lodge elder asks to meet you in a teahouse with three exits. "We are not your enemy," the elder says, pouring. "We are the only people in this world who know what everything costs. Even you."

choices.text: Ask what you cost

effects.log: "Less than you think," says the elder, "and more than they pay you." The tea is very good.

choices.text: Leave before the tea is poured

effects.log: You go out by the third door. Nobody follows. That is somehow worse.

events.text: The day the Lodge War ends, the markets of {pw_kingdom} open without anyone collecting at the gate. A baker gives you a loaf and will not take a copper. A ferry child asks if it is true that you did it. The road-singers already have the first verse.

choices.text: Say many people did it

effects.log: The child decides you are being modest, which makes the story better.

choices.text: Say yes

effects.log: The child runs off to tell everyone. By evening it is true in every tavern of the river towns.

events.text: When the war is over, the guild-mother who wrote your name in her book comes to your door with the book. Every page is a lock, a ward, a cure or a watchman, and a date. "Yours," she says. "I thought you should see what it added up to."

choices.text: Read it all, slowly

effects.log: It adds up to a great deal. You did not know until now.

choices.text: Give it back to her for the guild

effects.log: "Then the next one will know how it is done," she says, and takes it home.

events.text: The Lodge War is over and the Lodges won it. They are polite about it. A runner brings you a ledger with your own name in it and a very reasonable sum. "For the years ahead," the runner says. "Everyone pays. It is quieter that way."

choices.text: Pay, and hate it

effects.log: You pay. It is quieter that way. You hate every quiet day of it.

choices.text: Refuse, and keep refusing

effects.log: You refuse. Nothing happens for a year. Then a window breaks, and you refuse again.

events.text: With the Lodges holding the river gates, the king of {pw_kingdom} sends a cart of silver under their flag, by their road. The old people in the market watch it go and say nothing. A boy throws a stone at it, and his mother pulls him home.

choices.text: Find the boy, and teach him patience

effects.log: You find him the next day. You teach him to wait for the right stone.

choices.text: Write down what you saw

effects.log: You write it down. One day someone will want to know how it was.

events.text: The elders of the great house receive your gifts in a long hall with a fire at each end. Nobody looks at the gifts. Everybody looks at you: your hands, your clothes, the way you sit. A very old woman at the far end smiles once, as if a question has been answered.

choices.text: Sit as you always sit

effects.log: You sit as you always sit. The old woman smiles again. You have no idea why, and suspect it is good.

choices.text: Ask the old woman what she saw

effects.log: "A person who can be kind in a room full of strangers," she says. "That is rarer than silver."

events.text: A younger cousin of the great house catches you in the yard after your call. "They will offer you someone," the cousin says. "Everyone else in the house is a person too. Remember that, when you have four of us."

choices.text: Promise to remember

effects.log: The cousin nods, and does not quite believe you, and goes back in.

choices.text: Say you are only calling on one house

effects.log: "Everyone says that," says the cousin, not unkindly.

events.text: {npc} arrives with the house's banner, a cart of gifts and a very straight back. Your household is lined up at the door and pretending not to stare. {npc} looks at all of them, then at you. "I was told you were difficult," {he} says. "Good. So am I."

choices.text: Laugh, and take {his} hands

effects.log: {npc} does not laugh, but {his} hands are warm, and {he} does not let go first.

choices.text: Show {him} the house, room by room

effects.log: It takes all afternoon. By the kitchen {npc} has opinions; by the garden, plans.

events.text: The first evening {npc} is in your house, the others who share it come to the table one by one, and sit, and wait to see what kind of person the great house has sent. {npc} pours everyone's tea before {his} own.

choices.text: Thank {him} in front of everyone

effects.log: A small thing. The table breathes out. It is going to be all right, probably.

choices.text: Say nothing, and watch

effects.log: You watch. By the third cup, two of the others are arguing with {npc} about rice. That is a good sign.
